newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Sixt sees sales, profit up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: German Sixt sees sales, profit up in 1997.

text.p: German car rental group Sixt AG said on Tuesday it expected ongoing sales growth and even stronger profit growth this year after earnings surged in 1996.

The company also said it it was considering issuing bonus shares to allow shareholders to benefit from the strong 1996 performance. Sixt said it would leave its dividend unchanged at 14 marks per ordinary share and 15 marks per preference share.
Group profits surged in 1996, with earnings from ordinary activities up 67 percent at 46.3 million marks.
Sales rose to 2.1 billion marks from 1.7 billion the previous year and earnings per share jumped to 44.20 marks from 27.10 marks.
"The first two months of the year confirms the good developments of 1996 with double-digit growth in sales and rental data," Sixt said.
Sixt noted that its market share in car rentals had jumped to 24 percent from four percent ten years ago. The company is also Germany's leading used car dealer.
As well as the bonus share issue, which is subject to shareholder approval, Sixt said it would consider a capital increase.
The decision would be made on the basis of the Sixt share valuation and the market climate, Sixt said.
